AccessRestriction.description: An access restriction is a marking definition that describes a security, licensing, classification, operational security, or legal authority constraint on the use of a forensic tool capability. It is a subclass of uco-marking:MarkingDefinition because access restrictions are a specific form of data marking that conveys restrictions, permissions, and guidance for how capability data can be used and shared — the same semantic purpose served by UCO's marking namespace. By subclassing MarkingDefinition, access restrictions integrate into UCO's standard marking pipeline: they can be applied to any UcoObject via the objectMarking property, and they inherit the definitionType property which aligns with restrictionType. The toolcap-specific properties (restrictionType, restrictionLevel, restrictionDescription) provide forensic-domain refinement beyond what the base MarkingDefinition offers. When a specific investigative authorization is required, the restriction can link to a case-investigation:Authorization instance via requiredAuthorization. See https://www.nist.gov/publications for related information security marking standards.

BenchmarkObservation.description: A benchmark observation is a single point-in-time record of testing a forensic tool's capability. It is a subclass of uco-core:Assertion because each observation is an empirical assertion about a tool's performance that is declared to be true by the benchmarking party. Each observation captures the results of one test run, including pass/fail outcome, completeness and accuracy metrics, standard information retrieval metrics (precision, recall, F1), confusion matrix counts (TP, FP, FN), processing performance, benchmark provenance (framework name, test case identifier, suite score), observable categories parsed or missed, tool and application versions tested, and the data format version. BenchmarkObservation instances are append-only: new test runs produce new instances rather than updating existing ones, preserving a full audit trail of capability evidence over time. The inherited uco-core:statement property from Assertion may carry a human-readable summary of the benchmark result. See https://doi.org/10.6028/NIST.SP.500-281 for the NIST CFTT benchmark methodology.

properties.description: Free-text notes about this benchmark run.

properties.name: benchmarkSuiteScore
properties.description: An overall composite score from the benchmark framework, 0.0 to 1.0.

properties.name: benchmarkedBy
properties.description: Identifies the person or organization (an instance of uco-core:IdentityAbstraction) that performed this benchmark test.

properties.name: capability
properties.description: Links a BenchmarkObservation to the Capability it provides evidence for. In v0.4.0 the range is the generic capability:Capability class.

properties.name: completenessScore
properties.description: The fraction of expected records the tool successfully recovered, 0.0 to 1.0.

properties.name: datasetSizeInBytes
properties.description: Size of the test dataset in bytes.

properties.name: f1Score
properties.description: F1 = 2 * precision * recall / (precision + recall), 0.0 to 1.0.

properties.name: falseNegativeCount
properties.description: The number of items in the source data not recovered by the tool.

properties.name: falsePositiveCount
properties.description: The number of items the tool reported that do not actually exist in the source data.

properties.name: groundTruthCount
properties.description: The total number of items in the ground truth dataset.

properties.name: missedCategory
properties.description: An observable category the tool failed to extract despite data being present.

properties.name: parseSuccess
properties.description: A boolean indicating whether the tool produced any usable output in this benchmark run.

properties.name: parsedCategory
properties.description: An observable category successfully extracted in this benchmark run.

properties.name: precisionScore
properties.description: Precision = TP / (TP + FP), 0.0 to 1.0.

properties.name: processingDuration
properties.description: Wall-clock time for the benchmark run, expressed as xsd:duration.

properties.name: recallScore
properties.description: Recall = TP / (TP + FN), 0.0 to 1.0.

properties.name: submittedCount
properties.description: The total number of items reported by the tool. submittedCount = TP + FP.

properties.name: testCaseIdentifier
properties.description: A unique identifier for the specific test case within the benchmark framework.

properties.name: testedApplicationVersion
properties.description: The version of the target application whose data was used in this benchmark run.

properties.name: testedDataFormatVersion
properties.description: The data storage format version tested (e.g., '.pst', '.nst', 'SQLite WAL v2').

properties.name: testedToolVersion
properties.description: The exact version string of the forensic tool used in this benchmark run.

properties.name: truePositiveCount
properties.description: The number of items correctly identified by the tool.

properties.name: modifiedTime
properties.description: Specifies the time that this particular version of the object was modified. The object creator can use the time it deems most appropriate as the time this version of the object was modified. The value of the modified property for a given object version MUST be later than or equal to the value of the created property. Object creators MUST update the modified property when creating a new version of an object. The modified timestamp MUST be precise to the nearest millisecond (exactly three digits after the decimal place in seconds).

Capability.description: A capability is the ability of an entity to perform some action or produce some result. Capabilities are connected to their possessors (tools, modules, parsers, people, organizations) via uco-core:Relationship instances with kindOfRelationship='hasCapability'. A capability may be described unstructured (via name/description) or structured (via structuredCharacterization pointing to an ActionPattern). See https://github.com/ucoProject/UCO/issues/596 for related Software hierarchy work.

Structurally distinct from a single threat-delivery event; the cycle has no natural termination except apprehension or removal of material. properties.name: sustainedBy

properties.name: terminationCondition
properties.description: How the coercion cycle ended if known (apprehension, material_removal, victim_ceased_response, unknown).

properties.name: csaSchedule
properties.description: The controlled-substance schedule assigned in the governing jurisdiction, as an open vocabulary. Recommended values for the U.S. Controlled Substances Act: 'I', 'II', 'III', 'IV', 'V' (21 U.S.C. § 812, https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/21/812). Non-U.S. regimes may record their own designations, e.g. 'UK Class A'.

properties.name: mass
properties.description: The measured or charged mass of the portion, in the unit given by massUnit. For threshold quantities charged in the alternative ('500 grams or more'), record the threshold and keep the verbatim charging language in quantityDescription.

properties.name: massUnit
properties.description: The unit of the mass value, as a UCUM code (https://ucum.org/ucum), e.g. 'g', 'kg', 'mg'.

properties.name: purity
properties.description: Laboratory-determined purity of the portion as a percentage (0-100) of the controlled substance in the mixture.

properties.name: purityBasis
properties.description: Whether recorded quantities describe the whole mixture or the actual controlled substance it contains, as an open vocabulary. Recommended values: 'mixture' (a mixture or substance containing a detectable amount), 'actual' (the weight of the controlled substance itself). This distinction drives U.S. statutory thresholds (21 U.S.C. § 841(b)) and USSG § 2D1.1 offense levels (https://www.ussc.gov/guidelines).

properties.name: quantityDescription
properties.description: The quantity as stated verbatim in the source record, to avoid fabricating precision, e.g. '500 grams or more of a mixture and substance containing a detectable amount of methamphetamine'.

properties.name: substanceForm
properties.description: The physical form of the portion, as an open vocabulary. Recommended values: 'powder', 'crystal', 'tablet', 'capsule', 'liquid', 'plant-material', 'blotter', 'residue'.

properties.name: substanceName
properties.description: The substance name as recorded in the source record, kept verbatim, e.g. 'methamphetamine', 'a mixture and substance containing a detectable amount of methamphetamine'.

properties.name: chargeCount
properties.description: The total number of criminal charges associated with a ConvictionRecord or LegalProceeding (aggregate total, not the ordinal of a single count). Constrained on ConvictionRecord by ConvictionRecordShape (minInclusive 1, maxInclusive 100). Distinct from countNumber, which is the ordinal count number within a charging instrument. NOTE: some existing example graphs historically used chargeCount on individual CriminalCharge nodes as an ordinal; that usage SHOULD migrate to countNumber in a follow-up (this declaration does not rewrite those examples).

properties.name: convictionDate
properties.description: Date and time when the conviction was entered (verdict, acceptance of plea, or equivalent disposition). Required by ConvictionRecordShape as xsd:dateTime.

properties.name: convictionType
properties.description: How the conviction was obtained. Allowed values (ConvictionRecordShape): jury_verdict, bench_trial, plea_agreement, default_judgment, summary_conviction.

properties.name: priorConvictions
properties.description: Number of prior criminal convictions associated with the subject of this ConvictionRecord (aggregate count for history context; 0–50 per ConvictionRecordShape). Use non-graphic, structured counts only.

CryptocurrencyAddressFacet.description: A cryptocurrency address facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to a blockchain address used to send and receive virtual assets on a distributed ledger network. A virtual currency address is roughly equivalent to an anonymous account number and has a corresponding private key needed to spend value held at the address (see the affidavit in United States v. Lichtenstein, No. 1:23-cr-00239-CKK (D.D.C.), Statement of Facts nn.4-9, and the INTERPOL DW-VA Taxonomy entity 'wallet': https://interpol-innovation-centre.github.io/DW-VA-Taxonomy/taxonomies/entities#wallet). Attach to a uco-observable:ObservableObject via uco-core:hasFacet.

properties.name: addressFormat
properties.description: The encoding format of the address as an open vocabulary. Recommended values: 'Base58Check', 'Bech32', 'Hex'. See BIP-173 (https://github.com/bitcoin/bips/blob/master/bip-0173.mediawiki) for Bech32 and https://en.bitcoin.it/wiki/Base58Check_encoding for Base58Check.

properties.name: addressValue
properties.description: The cryptocurrency address string, e.g. '1CGA4s...' (Base58Check), 'bc1q...' (Bech32), or '0x8CE693CB0626924583931F25f50AF8fC1C6517F0' (Ethereum hex). See Bitcoin address encodings in BIP-173 (https://github.com/bitcoin/bips/blob/master/bip-0173.mediawiki).

properties.name: blockchainNetwork
properties.description: The distributed ledger network the address or transaction belongs to, e.g. 'Bitcoin Mainnet', 'Ethereum', 'Litecoin'. A blockchain is a public transaction ledger that includes a record of every transaction that has ever occurred on the network (https://interpol-innovation-centre.github.io/DW-VA-Taxonomy/taxonomies/entities#blockchain).

properties.name: cryptocurrencyType
properties.description: The type of cryptocurrency, as an open vocabulary of ticker symbols. Recommended values: BTC, ETH, LTC, XMR, ZEC, DASH, ETC, BCH, BSV, BTG, XRP, DOGE, SOL, ADA, DOT, AVAX, MATIC, USDT, USDC, WETH. Producers may use identifiers not in this list to accommodate new virtual assets (ticker symbols as listed by major data providers, e.g. https://coinmarketcap.com/).

CryptocurrencyInfrastructure.description: Cryptocurrency wallets, exchanges, and payment processing systems used for anonymous financial transactions (gUFO FunctionalComplex).

CryptocurrencyMixingService.description: A cryptocurrency mixing service (mixer or tumbler) obscures the link between transaction inputs and outputs by combining or shuffling the virtual assets of multiple users — for example via coinjoin, a method where two or more user transactions are combined into a single blockchain transaction with multiple inputs and outputs (INTERPOL DW-VA Taxonomy: https://interpol-innovation-centre.github.io/DW-VA-Taxonomy/taxonomies/entities#coinjoin). Examples cited in federal prosecutions include Bitcoin Fog, Helix, and ChipMixer (United States v. Lichtenstein, No. 1:23-cr-00239-CKK (D.D.C.), Statement of the Offense para. 19; see also FinCEN guidance FIN-2019-G001, https://www.fincen.gov/resources/statutes-and-regulations/guidance).

CryptocurrencyTransactionFacet.description: A cryptocurrency transaction facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to a transfer of value recorded on a blockchain distributed ledger. Attach to a uco-observable:ObservableObject representing the transaction; model the source and destination addresses as uco-observable:ObservableRelationship instances with uco-core:kindOfRelationship values 'Transaction_Input' and 'Transaction_Output' and a cryptoinv:transferAmount. This pattern natively supports UTXO-chain transactions (Bitcoin) with multiple inputs and outputs (see https://developer.bitcoin.org/devguide/transactions.html) as well as account-based chains (Ethereum).

properties.name: blockHash
properties.description: The hash of the block containing this transaction (https://developer.bitcoin.org/reference/block_chain.html).

properties.name: blockNumber
properties.description: The block number (block height) in the blockchain at which the transaction was confirmed (https://developer.bitcoin.org/reference/block_chain.html).

properties.name: confirmationCount
properties.description: The number of blockchain confirmations at the time of observation. This is a point-in-time snapshot, not a time-varying quality (time-varying properties are deferred to https://github.com/ucoProject/UCO/issues/535).

properties.name: transactionFee
properties.description: The transaction fee in the native cryptocurrency unit of the network (https://developer.bitcoin.org/devguide/transactions.html#transaction-fees-and-change).

properties.name: transactionHash
properties.description: The unique hash identifier of the blockchain transaction, e.g. '6e0d701ac2ea3ad87fc8bcaa786b994aa943f5eb9a67a1e345769bb090bf5b9e' (a Bitcoin transaction identifier / txid; see https://developer.bitcoin.org/reference/transactions.html).

properties.name: transactionStatus
properties.description: The status of the transaction at the time of observation, as an open vocabulary. Recommended values: 'Confirmed', 'Pending', 'Failed'.

properties.name: transactionType
properties.description: The investigative characterization of the transaction, as an open vocabulary. Recommended values: 'Transfer', 'Exchange', 'Purchase', 'Mixing', 'Withdrawal', 'Deposit', 'ContractExecution', 'Staking', 'Unstaking'. Mixing and chain-hopping transaction types are defined in the INTERPOL DW-VA Taxonomy (https://interpol-innovation-centre.github.io/DW-VA-Taxonomy/taxonomies/entities#coinjoin).

CryptocurrencyWalletFacet.description: A cryptocurrency wallet facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to a wallet: software, a device, or a hosted service that keeps track of the private keys used to sign virtual-asset transactions, and which may contain many virtual currency addresses (INTERPOL DW-VA Taxonomy: https://interpol-innovation-centre.github.io/DW-VA-Taxonomy/taxonomies/entities#wallet). First proposed as CryptoWalletFacet in https://github.com/casework/CASE/issues/87; this revision omits time-varying balance properties, which remain blocked by https://github.com/ucoProject/UCO/issues/535 — use cryptoinv:VirtualAssetHoldingFacet for point-in-time holdings snapshots.

properties.name: addressCount
properties.description: The number of virtual currency addresses contained in the wallet at the time of observation (a wallet may include many addresses, each with a corresponding private key).

properties.name: walletIdentifier
properties.description: An investigative identifier for the wallet or address cluster, e.g. the first characters of a representative address ('Wallet 1CGA4s') or a chain-analysis cluster label ('Cluster 36B6mu'). A cluster is a grouping of addresses believed to be contained within a single wallet (United States v. Lichtenstein, No. 1:23-cr-00239-CKK (D.D.C.), Statement of Facts n.28).

properties.name: walletType
properties.description: The custody model and form factor of the wallet, as an open vocabulary. Recommended values: 'hosted' (a third party retains the customer's funds: https://interpol-innovation-centre.github.io/DW-VA-Taxonomy/taxonomies/entities#hosted-wallet), 'unhosted' (the user exercises total, independent control over funds: https://interpol-innovation-centre.github.io/DW-VA-Taxonomy/taxonomies/entities#unhosted-wallet), 'hardware' (https://interpol-innovation-centre.github.io/DW-VA-Taxonomy/taxonomies/entities#hardware_wallet), 'software' (https://interpol-innovation-centre.github.io/DW-VA-Taxonomy/taxonomies/entities#software_wallet), 'paper'.

CustodialAbuse.description: Abuse committed by someone in custodial or caregiving role. Modeled as gUFO SubKind of TrustViolation with role-based context.

properties.name: hasViolationBeginPoint
properties.description: Temporal begin point when trust violation started.

properties.name: hasViolationEndPoint
properties.description: Temporal end point when trust violation ceased.

properties.name: perpetratedBy
properties.description: Links trust violation to the authority figure who perpetrated it. Enhanced with gUFO event participation patterns.

properties.name: violationSeverity
properties.description: Severity level of trust violation (minor, moderate, severe, extreme).

properties.name: violationType
properties.description: Type of trust violation (abuse_of_authority, breach_of_care, exploitation, negligence).

CustodialAuthorization.description: Official authorization granting custodial rights or responsibilities. Modeled as gUFO Object with legal authority.

properties.name: execProgramHashes
properties.description: Specifies the hashes of the executable file launched by the action.

properties.description: Specifies the path to the executable file launched by the action. See also: http://msdn.microsoft.com/en-us/library/windows/desktop/aa380715(v=vs.85).aspx.

properties.name: execWorkingDirectory
properties.description: Specifies the directory that contains either the executable file or the files that are used by the executable file launched by the action. See also: http://msdn.microsoft.com/en-us/library/windows/desktop/aa380715(v=vs.85).aspx.

In forensic tool architectures, a module represents a pluggable unit of functionality such as a parsing module, carving module, or decryption module. properties.name: arguments
properties.description: A list of arguments utilized in initiating the process.

properties.description: The user that created/owns the process.

properties.description: A small number passed from the process to the parent process when it has finished executing. In general, 0 indicates successful termination, any other number indicates a failure.

properties.description: The isHidden property specifies whether the process is hidden or not.

properties.name: parent

properties.name: pid
properties.description: The Process ID, or PID, of the process.

properties.name: status
properties.description: Specifies a list of statuses for a given Whois entry.

ProcessThread.description: A process thread is the smallest sequence of programmed instructions that can be managed independently by a scheduler on a computer, which is typically a part of the operating system. It is a component of a process. Multiple threads can exist within one process, executing concurrently and sharing resources such as memory, while different processes do not share these resources. In particular, the threads of a process share its executable code and the values of its dynamically allocated variables and non-thread-local global variables at any given time. [based on https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thread_(computing)]

RacketeeringEnterprise.description: A racketeering enterprise is an 'enterprise' as defined in 18 U.S.C. § 1961(4) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/18/1961): any individual, partnership, corporation, association, or other legal entity, and any union or group of individuals associated in fact although not a legal entity, whose affairs are conducted or participated in through a pattern of racketeering activity (18 U.S.C. § 1962, https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/18/1962). An association-in-fact enterprise must have a purpose, relationships among those associated with the enterprise, and longevity sufficient to permit the associates to pursue the enterprise's purpose (Boyle v. United States, 556 U.S. 938 (2009), https://supreme.justia.com/cases/federal/us/556/938/). Record the charged purposes and the interstate/foreign commerce nexus in uco-core:description; record membership with uco-core:Relationship nodes of kind 'Member_Of' from persons to the enterprise; record the charged operating span with existence-interval or description conventions.

The object creator can use the time it deems most appropriate as the time this version of the object was modified. The value of the modified property for a given object version MUST be later than or equal to the value of the created property. Object creators MUST update the modified property when creating a new version of an object. The modified timestamp MUST be precise to the nearest millisecond (exactly three digits after the decimal place in seconds).

properties.description: Specifies the time that this particular version of the object was modified. The modified timestamp MUST be precise to the nearest millisecond (exactly three digits after the decimal place in seconds).

The object creator can use the time it deems most appropriate as the time this version of the object was modified. The value of the modified property for a given object version MUST be later than or equal to the value of the created property. Object creators MUST update the modified property when creating a new version of an object. The modified timestamp MUST be precise to the nearest millisecond (exactly three digits after the decimal place in seconds).

properties.name: modifiedTime
properties.description: Specifies the time that this particular version of the object was modified. VirtualAssetHoldingFacet.description: A virtual asset holding facet is a grouping of characteristics describing a point-in-time quantity of a specific virtual asset held at, contained in, or seized from a wallet, address, or account — for example 'approximately 94,636 BTC seized on 2022-02-01, valued at $3.629 billion' (United States v. Lichtenstein, No. 1:23-cr-00239-CKK (D.D.C.), Statement of Facts para. 6). Each holding is an observation snapshot with an optional fiat valuation, deliberately avoiding the time-varying balance problem deferred to https://github.com/ucoProject/UCO/issues/535.

properties.name: assetQuantity
properties.description: The quantity of the virtual asset in its native unit at the observation time, e.g. 94643.29837084.

properties.name: assetSymbol
properties.description: The ticker symbol of the held virtual asset, as an open vocabulary (same recommended values as cryptoinv:cryptocurrencyType, plus platform tokens such as aUSDC, aUSDT, yvUSDT).

properties.name: fiatCurrencyCode
properties.description: The ISO 4217 alphabetic currency code of the fiat valuation, e.g. 'USD' (https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html).

properties.name: fiatValue
properties.description: The fiat-currency valuation of the holding at the valuation date. Fiat money is a currency established as money by government regulation (https://interpol-innovation-centre.github.io/DW-VA-Taxonomy/taxonomies/entities#fiat-money).

properties.name: valuationDate
properties.description: The date and time at which the fiat valuation of the holding was made. The trading value of virtual assets fluctuates over time depending on market demand.

VirtualAssetServiceProvider.description: A virtual asset service provider (VASP) is any natural or legal person who as a business conducts one or more of the following activities for or on behalf of another natural or legal person: exchange between virtual assets and fiat currencies; exchange between one or more forms of virtual assets; transfer of virtual assets; safekeeping and/or administration of virtual assets or instruments enabling control over virtual assets; and participation in and provision of financial services related to an issuer's offer and/or sale of a virtual asset (FATF definition, as recorded in the INTERPOL DW-VA Taxonomy: https://interpol-innovation-centre.github.io/DW-VA-Taxonomy/taxonomies/entities#VASP). Virtual currency exchanges (VCEs) doing business in the United States are regulated by the U.S. Department of the Treasury and must establish anti-money-laundering programs under the Bank Secrecy Act (31 U.S.C. § 5311 et seq., https://www.fincen.gov/resources/statutes-and-regulations/bank-secrecy-act).

VirtualizedComputer.description: A computer (desktop, laptop, or server) that exists as a virtual machine rather than running on physical hardware. The most common form is a server running as a virtual machine in a datacentre or cloud environment, which may itself be the subject of an investigation or host evidence. In a forensic context a virtualized computer may also, for example, be a virtual machine recovered from seized media, a forensic disk image booted as a virtual machine for previewing, or a virtual machine provisioned as an analysis environment.

VirtualizedDevice.description: A device or system that exists as a virtual machine, defined by virtualization configuration and one or more virtual disks rather than running on dedicated physical hardware. A virtualized device may arise in several ways, for example a virtual machine recovered from a suspect's storage, a forensic image booted as a virtual machine for previewing, or a virtual machine built as an analysis platform. This is the parent class for virtualized representations of any device type (e.g. computers, mobile devices).

properties.name: domainID

properties.name: domainName

properties.name: expirationDate

properties.name: serverName

properties.name: sponsoringRegistrar

properties.name: status
properties.description: Specifies a list of statuses for a given Whois entry.

properties.name: updatedDate

properties.name: lastName

properties.name: middleName

properties.name: namePhonetic

WindowsCriticalSection.description: A Windows critical section is a Windows object that provides synchronization similar to that provided by a mutex object, except that a critical section can be used only by the threads of a single process. Critical section objects cannot be shared across processes. Event, mutex, and semaphore objects can also be used in a single-process application, but critical section objects provide a slightly faster, more efficient mechanism for mutual-exclusion synchronization (a processor-specific test and set instruction). Like a mutex object, a critical section object can be owned by only one thread at a time, which makes it useful for protecting a shared resource from simultaneous access. Unlike a mutex object, there is no way to tell whether a critical section has been abandoned. [based on https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/sync/critical-section-objects]

WindowsFilemapping.description: A Windows file mapping is the association of a file's contents with a portion of the virtual address space of a process within a Windows operating system. The system creates a file mapping object (also known as a section object) to maintain this association. A file view is the portion of virtual address space that a process uses to access the file's contents. File mapping allows the process to use both random input and output (I/O) and sequential I/O. It also allows the process to work efficiently with a large data file, such as a database, without having to map the whole file into memory. Multiple processes can also use memory-mapped files to share data. Processes read from and write to the file view using pointers, just as they would with dynamically allocated memory. The use of file mapping improves efficiency because the file resides on disk, but the file view resides in memory.[based on https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/memory/file-mapping]

properties.name: numberOfSymbols
properties.description: Specifies the number of entries in the symbol table of the PE binary, as a non-negative integer.

properties.name: optionalHeader
properties.description: Specifies the PE optional header of the PE binary.

properties.name: peType
properties.description: Specifies the type of the PE binary.

properties.name: pointerToSymbolTable
properties.description: Specifies the file offset of the COFF symbol table.

properties.name: sections
properties.description: Specifies metadata about the sections in the PE file.

properties.name: sizeOfOptionalHeader
properties.description: Specifies the size of the optional header of the PE binary.

properties.name: timeDateStamp
properties.description: Specifies the time when the PE binary was created.

WindowsPEFileHeader.description: A Windows PE file header is a grouping of characteristics unique to the 'header' of a Windows PE (Portable Executable) file, consisting of a collection of metadata about the overall nature and structure of the file.

properties.name: timeDateStamp
properties.description: Specifies the time when the PE binary was created.

WindowsPEOptionalHeader.description: A Windows PE optional header is a grouping of characteristics unique to the 'optional header' of a Windows PE (Portable Executable) file, consisting of a collection of metadata about the executable code structure of the file.

properties.name: addressOfEntryPoint
properties.description: Specifies the address of the entry point relative to the image base when the executable is loaded into memory.

properties.name: baseOfCode
properties.description: Specifies the address that is relative to the image base of the beginning-of-code section when it is loaded into memory.

properties.name: checksum
properties.description: Specifies the checksum of the PE binary.

properties.name: dllCharacteristics
properties.description: Specifies the flags that characterize the PE binary.

properties.name: fileAlignment
properties.description: Specifies the factor (in bytes) that is used to align the raw data of sections in the image file.

properties.name: imageBase
properties.description: Specifies the address that is relative to the image base of the beginning-of-data section when it is loaded into memory.

properties.name: loaderFlags
properties.description: Specifies the reserved loader flags

properties.name: magic
properties.description: Specifies the value that indicates the type of the PE binary.

properties.name: majorImageVersion
properties.description: Specifies the major version number of the image.

properties.name: majorLinkerVersion
properties.description: Specifies the linker major version number.

properties.name: majorOSVersion
properties.description: Specifies the major version number of the required operating system.

properties.name: majorSubsystemVersion
properties.description: Specifies the major version number of the subsystem.

properties.name: minorImageVersion
properties.description: Specifies the minor version number of the image.

properties.name: minorLinkerVersion
properties.description: Specifies the linker minor version number.

properties.name: minorOSVersion
properties.description: Specifies the minor version number of the required operating system.

properties.name: minorSubsystemVersion
properties.description: Specifies the minor version number of the subsystem.

properties.name: numberOfRVAAndSizes
properties.description: Specifies the number of data-directory entries in the remainder of the optional header.

properties.name: sectionAlignment
properties.description: Specifies the alignment (in bytes) of PE sections when they are loaded into memory.

properties.name: sizeOfCode
properties.description: Specifies the size of the code (text) section. If there are multiple such sections, this refers to the sum of the sizes of each section.

properties.name: sizeOfHeaders
properties.description: Specifies the combined size of the MS-DOS, PE header, and section headers, rounded up a multiple of the value specified in the file_alignment header.

properties.name: sizeOfHeapCommit
properties.description: Specifies the size of the local heap space to commit.

properties.name: sizeOfHeapReserve
properties.description: Specifies the size of the local heap space to reserve.

properties.name: sizeOfImage
properties.description: Specifies the size, in bytes, of the image, including all headers, as the image is loaded in memory.

properties.name: sizeOfInitializedData
properties.description: Specifies the size of the initialized data section. If there are multiple such sections, this refers to the sum of the sizes of each section.

properties.name: sizeOfStackCommit
properties.description: Specifies the size of the stack to commit.

properties.name: sizeOfStackReserve
properties.description: Specifies the size of the stack to reserve.

properties.name: sizeOfUninitializedData
properties.description: Specifies the size of the uninitialized data section. If there are multiple such sections, this refers to the sum of the sizes of each section.

properties.name: subsystem
properties.description: Specifies the subsystem (e.g., GUI, device driver, etc.) that is required to run this image.

properties.name: win32VersionValue
properties.description: Specifies the reserved win32 version value.

WindowsPESection.description: A Windows PE section is a grouping of characteristics unique to a specific default or custom-defined region of a Windows PE (Portable Executable) file, consisting of an individual portion of the actual executable content of the file delineated according to unique purpose and memory protection requirements.

properties.name: name
properties.description: The name of a particular concept characterization.

properties.name: entropy
properties.description: Shannon entropy (a measure of randomness) of the data.

properties.name: hashes
properties.description: Specifies any hashes computed over the section.

properties.name: size
properties.description: Specifies the size of the section, in bytes.

WindowsTaskFacet.description: A Windows Task facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to a Windows Task (a process that is scheduled to execute on a Windows operating system by the Windows Task Scheduler). [based on http://msdn.microsoft.com/en-us/library/windows/desktop/aa381311(v=vs.85).aspx]

properties.name: account
properties.description: Specifies the account referenced in an event log entry or used to run the scheduled task. See also: http://msdn.microsoft.com/en-us/library/windows/desktop/aa381228(v=vs.85).aspx.

properties.name: accountLogonType
properties.description: Specifies the security logon method required to run the tasks associated with the account. See also: http://msdn.microsoft.com/en-us/library/windows/desktop/aa383013(v=vs.85).aspx.

properties.name: accountRunLevel
properties.description: Specifies the permission level of the account that the task will be run at.

properties.name: actionList
properties.description: Specifies a list of actions to be performed by the scheduled task.

properties.name: application
properties.description: The application associated with this object.

properties.name: exitCode
properties.description: Specifies the last exit code of the scheduled task. See also: http://msdn.microsoft.com/en-us/library/windows/desktop/aa381245(v=vs.85).aspx.

properties.name: flags
properties.description: Specifies any flags that modify the behavior of the scheduled task. See also: http://msdn.microsoft.com/en-us/library/windows/desktop/aa381248(v=vs.85).aspx.

properties.name: imageName
properties.description: Specifies the image name for the task.

properties.name: maxRunTime
properties.description: Specifies the maximum run time of the scheduled task before terminating, in milliseconds. See also: http://msdn.microsoft.com/en-us/library/windows/desktop/aa381874(v=vs.85).aspx.

properties.name: mostRecentRunTime
properties.description: Specifies the most recent run date/time of this scheduled task. See also: http://msdn.microsoft.com/en-us/library/windows/desktop/aa381254(v=vs.85).aspx.

properties.name: nextRunTime
properties.description: Specifies the next run date/time of the scheduled task. See also: http://msdn.microsoft.com/en-us/library/windows/desktop/aa381257(v=vs.85).aspx.

properties.name: observableCreatedTime
properties.description: The date and time at which the observable object being characterized was created. This time pertains to an intrinsic characteristic of the observable object, and would be consistent across independent characterizations or observations of the observable object.

properties.name: parameters
properties.description: Specifies the command line parameters used to launch the scheduled task. See also: http://msdn.microsoft.com/en-us/library/windows/desktop/aa381875(v=vs.85).aspx.

properties.name: priority
properties.description: The priority of the email.

properties.name: status
properties.description: Specifies a list of statuses for a given Whois entry.

properties.name: taskComment
properties.description: Specifies a comment for the scheduled task. See also: http://msdn.microsoft.com/en-us/library/windows/desktop/aa381232(v=vs.85).aspx.

properties.name: taskCreator
properties.description: Specifies the name of the creator of the scheduled task. See also: http://msdn.microsoft.com/en-us/library/windows/desktop/aa381235(v=vs.85).aspx.

properties.name: triggerList
properties.description: Specifies a set of triggers used by the scheduled task. See also: http://msdn.microsoft.com/en-us/library/windows/desktop/aa383264(v=vs.85).aspx.

properties.name: workItemData
properties.description: Specifies application defined data associated with the scheduled task. See also: http://msdn.microsoft.com/en-us/library/windows/desktop/aa381271(v=vs.85).aspx.

properties.name: workingDirectory
properties.description: Specifies the working directory for the scheduled task. See also: http://msdn.microsoft.com/en-us/library/windows/desktop/aa381878(v=vs.85).aspx.
